papers.title: Impact of Circadian Adaptation on Sleep Architecture and Neurobehavioral Performance in Simulated Shiftwork.
papers.abstract: Shiftworkers rarely achieve full circadian adaptation to their schedule. We studied the impact of circadian misalignment on sleep and neurobehavioral performance using a simulated shiftwork paradigm. Nineteen individuals (mean±SD, 38±10 yrs, 10F) were studied in an 8-day inpatient protocol with a Baseline day (8h sleep), followed by an abrupt 8-hour delay shift in sleep-wake timing maintained for four days (simulated shiftwork) paired with different ambient lighting conditions to promote circadian adaptation, then a 30-hour constant routine (CR). Circadian adaptation was measured using the change in Dim Light Melatonin Onset between Baseline and CR. Sleep was recorded by polysomnography; subjective sleepiness and neurocognitive performance were assessed at regular intervals. Daytime sleep following the final nightshift had significant reductions in total sleep time (TST), stage 2 sleep, sleep efficiency (SE), and an increase in wake after sleep onset (WASO) compared to Baseline (p<0.05). Greater circadian adaptation was significantly correlated with higher TST (r2=0.37, p<0.01), REM sleep (r2=0.37, p<0.01), and SE (r2=0.48, p<0.01), and less WASO (r2=0.53, p<0.01). More slow-wave sleep correlated with a higher PRM score and less sleepiness (both, p≤0.03). More circadian adaptation was associated with better sleep architecture, less sleepiness, and better neurobehavioral performance. Interventions to facilitate circadian adaptation, such as appropriately timed-light exposure, could improve sleep and performance in shiftworkers.

papers.title: Hemodynamic spectral signatures across vigilance states: a whole-night EEG/fNIRS investigation.
papers.abstract: Sleep is accompanied by coordinated changes in neuronal activity and cerebral hemodynamics. However, cortical hemodynamic signatures across sleep stages remain poorly characterized, partly because most human electroencephalography (EEG)/functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) studies are limited in duration, rarely capture deep or Rapid-Eye-Movement (REM) sleep, have low sampling rate, or rely on a sleep-deprivation paradigm, which limits the generalizability of findings. Here, we combined whole-night polysomnography, EEG and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) in healthy young adults, as a bedside technology to monitor cortical hemodynamic fluctuations. We recorded fNIRS using an optimal, personalized, locally dense bilateral frontoparietal montage, alongside peripheral physiology recordings (respiration, photoplethysmography, mean arterial pressure). We computed oscillatory components of oxy- and deoxyhemoglobin (HbO-HbR) spectra across sleep stages using wavelet-based time-frequency analysis. Additionally, we analyzed within the same regions an independent sleep EEG-fMRI dataset (no REM recorded). Our results are suggesting that across frontal and parietal regions, slow-frequency (0.002-0.1Hz) power increased during N1 sleep in HbO and then progressively attenuated across N2 and N3 sleep, in HbO, HbR, and fMRI. REM showed a re-emergence of very-low-frequency power (<0.01Hz) in HbO and HbR. Higher-frequency oscillations (0.15-0.5Hz; overlapping respiratory-band) were selectively enhanced during NREM sleep (largest increase during N3) and returned toward wake-like levels during REM in frontal regions, with regional differences. Peripheral signals captured systemic physiology oscillations but did not reproduce the cortical stage-specific patterns. Together, our findings provide a cortical characterization of sleep-stage hemodynamic organizations that can serve as a reference for future mechanistic and clinical sleep studies.

papers.title: Acoustic stimuli-enhanced environmental enrichment remodulates cortical processing of sound azimuth in adult female rats.
papers.abstract: Acoustic stimuli-enhanced environmental enrichment (AEE) has been shown to significantly facilitate the behavioral and neuronal processing of sound by promoting plasticity in the auditory system. However, the mechanisms through which acoustic stimulation contributes to enrichment-induced effects remain largely unexplored. Here we found that AEE exposure during adulthood significantly improved the sound-azimuth discrimination abilities of female rats compared to age-matched naïve controls. Furthermore, AEE enhanced the sound-azimuth selectivity of neurons in the primary auditory cortex. These changes in the behavioral and cortical processing of sound azimuth were accompanied by an increase in the density of cortical parvalbumin-labeled (PV+) inhibitory interneurons. Interestingly, the rats reared in an identical enriched condition but without extra sound exposure also exhibited sharper cortical azimuth tuning and more cortical PV+ interneurons compared to the naïve rats. However, the post-rearing effects in these rats were less pronounced than those observed in the AEE rats, indicating an additional contribution of acoustic stimulation to enrichment-induced changes in the mature auditory cortex. Together, these findings provide compelling evidence for the significant influence of AEE on behavioral and cortical processing of sound azimuth. They suggest that AEE is an effective paradigm for promoting experience-dependent plasticity in the auditory system, even beyond the traditionally recognized critical period.

papers.title: Effects of Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring During Polysomnography on Sleep Indices and EEG Power.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) may disturb sleep during polysomnography (PSG), and the first-night effect (FNE) can complicate interpretation. We evaluated changes associated with ABPM and FNE across whole nights and individual measurements. Methods: This secondary analysis included 72 nominally healthy adults in a balanced two-night crossover, with ABPM on one randomly assigned night. Linear mixed-effects models estimated associations with PSG-derived sleep indices, a composite sleep quality index (SQI), and relative electroencephalographic (EEG) power. Analyses of individual measurements summarized EEG changes, sleep-stage transitions, and automated arousal detections. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (BH-FDR) adjustment was applied within defined analysis families. Results: FNE and ABPM were associated with lower SQI (β = -0.049 and -0.051, respectively; both BH-adjusted p = 0.028). FNE was associated with altered sleep continuity and architecture, whereas ABPM was associated with higher light-sleep and lower N3-sleep percentages and higher whole-night relative theta power. In the Night 2 paired analysis, relative delta power was lower and relative alpha, beta, and gamma power were higher during ABPM than before ABPM (all BH-adjusted p < 0.01); the theta difference did not reach significance (BH-adjusted p = 0.0632). Of 655 eligible ABPM measurements beginning during sleep, 395 (60.3%) contained at least one arousal detection within the 2 min measurement window. Conclusions: These detections indicate temporal co-occurrence and do not establish that cuff inflation caused arousal. Concurrent ABPM and study-night order should be considered when interpreting PSG. An adaptation PSG night may be considered when feasible, as may cuffless blood pressure monitoring once its accuracy has been established for the intended setting.

papers.title: MM-SleepNet: An Automatic Sleep Staging Network Based on Modal Re-Weighting and Mamba.
papers.abstract: Sleep staging is the key step in sleep quality assessment and sleep disorder diagnosis. In clinical practice, doctors usually use polysomnography (PSG) to stage sleep. PSG contains physiological signals such as electroencephalography (EEG) and electrooculography (EOG) and is divided into continuous epochs of fixed duration. In order to achieve more efficient and accurate automatic interpretation of PSG, this paper proposes MM-SleepNet, an automatic sleep staging network based on modal re-weighting and Mamba. MM-SleepNet divides each epoch into several overlapping patches and uses a newly designed patch feature extractor to extract the features of each patch, in order to solve the problem of key waveforms in the patch being obscured by non-key waveforms throughout the epoch. Afterward, MM-SleepNet calculates the importance of different signals on patches at the same time point through a dynamic re-weighting module. MM-SleepNet uses a bidirectional Mamba encoder that considers positional encoding to learn contextual information across epochs to adapt to the transition patterns between sleep stages. The experimental results on the Sleep-EDF and ISRUC datasets show that the proposed MM-SleepNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods. In addition, ablation experiments have demonstrated the effectiveness of various modules in MM-SleepNet.

papers.title: Repairing the disruption of protein homeostasis ameliorates REM sleep dysfunction in mouse models of Huntington's disease.
papers.abstract: Although disruption of sleep behavior is prevalent across different neurodegenerative diseases, there is little understood about the molecular mechanisms that tie them together. To explore this relationship, we turned to the autosomal dominant disorder Huntington's disease (HD), which shares many features common to more prevalent sporadic diseases, such as abnormal protein accumulation, early cognitive changes, and cell type specific degeneration. Moreover, HD patients suffer from sleep disruption, which precedes the appearance of core clinical features of the disease. We have previously found that upregulation of selective autophagy can prevent the aberrant protein accumulation that is typical of HD and other disorders. Thus, given the robust modeling of HD, we performed sleep analysis in the presence or absence of the upregulation of selective autophagy, to test the hypothesis that the proteinopathy significantly contributes to sleep dysfunction. We found that HD mice display rapid eye movement (REM) sleep impairments and protein aggregation in sleep-related regions including the nucleus accumbens and amygdala. Augmenting selective autophagy in the brain slowed aberrant protein accumulation and ameliorated REM sleep deficits in HD mice. Taken together, these data suggest that the disruption of protein homeostasis may play a key role in sleep dysfunction and disease.

papers.title: Using hip-worn accelerometer non-wear time to assess sleep duration and sleep midpoint.
papers.abstract: We sought to validate non-wear time of accelerometers worn on the hip for all waking hours as an estimate of sleep duration and midpoint. If valid, this may allow research studies to leverage previously collected physical activity data for sleep research. In 2019-2023, 21,325 Cancer Prevention Study-3 participants (mean age 58 years, SD=9.8) were provided a hip-worn accelerometer and sleep diaries for a week. Time in bed (TIB) was defined as the duration of non-wear time between two consecutive wear days (e.g. wear on Monday and Tuesday correspond to Monday night sleep). A total of 17,855 participants had at least 3 weekday and 1 weekend sleep measurements. Bland-Altman plots compared TIB and midpoint calculated from accelerometer non-wear and from sleep diaries. Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated for TIB to assess convergent validity, and a Two One-Sided Test (TOST) was calculated for midpoint to assess equivalence (± 15 minutes). Participants were mostly non-Hispanic white (87%) and female (77%). On average, TIB was 41.1 (SD=44.6) minutes longer on weekdays (r = 0.72) and 41.3 (SD=61.0) minutes longer on weekend days (r = 0.67) compared to sleep diary. Accelerometry sleep midpoint was 1.3 minutes earlier compared to diary on weekdays and 1.6 minutes later on weekends (TOST p-value < 0.01). TIB calculated from non-wear time of hip accelerometry demonstrated convergent validity with sleep duration assessed from sleep diary. Midpoint based on non-wear time was equivalent to sleep diary.

papers.title: Effects of BL Exposure on Circadian Rhythms and Rhythm-Related Disorders.
papers.abstract: Circadian rhythms represent a core physiological mechanism sustaining human physiological homeostasis and normal bodily function. Environmental light serves as a primary exogenous zeitgeber for circadian regulation. Among visible light spectral components, BL (BL) exerts a critical modulatory influence on the circadian system, with dual implications for physiological regulation and clinical intervention: excessive or inappropriately timed exposure may lead to circadian disruption, whereas appropriately timed BL interventions show potential to improve circadian alignment in selected populations. Accumulated evidence indicates that circadian disruption is associated with sleep disorders, mood disturbances, neurodegenerative disorders, as well as metabolic and immune dysfunction, and may have bidirectional relationships with disease progression. Nevertheless, most existing studies concentrate on circadian modulation by broad-spectrum light. Few efforts have synthesized the molecular mechanisms, potential disease-related pathways, and targeted intervention frameworks of BL-associated circadian disruption, and the translational potential of BL's bidirectional effects remains under-summarized, forming a prominent research gap. To fill this gap, this narrative review centers on the "BL-circadian rhythm-disease" regulatory axis. It outlines biological pathways in which circadian disruption may be implicated in multiple neurodegenerative disorders, highlights the circadian-modulating properties of BL, describes evidence linking inappropriate BL exposure to circadian disruption and disease onset or progression, and compiles clinical findings on BL-based interventions and their potential benefits for circadian function and selected disease-related symptoms. However, much of the evidence derives from observational studies and animal experiments, and a causal pathway linking BL exposure to disease through circadian disruption has not been definitively established. This review discusses the potential adverse and beneficial effects of BL in circadian disruption-related pathologies, addresses current research limitations, and offers theoretical references and fresh insights for mechanistic investigations, clinical research, and translational development of BL-targeted interventions.

papers.title: The Circadian Diet in Age-Related Neurodegeneration: Nutrient Timing, Sleep, and Mitochondrial Mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Circadian rhythms coordinate sleep-wake regulation, endocrine secretion, nutrient handling and cellular energy metabolism. Circadian and sleep disturbances are associated with metabolic and cardiovascular morbidity and with neurodegenerative disorders, particularly Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD), although whether restoring circadian alignment modifies neurodegeneration remains uncertain. This narrative review examines chrononutrition within the broader context of sleep regulation, physical activity and circadian care, distinguishing evidence from cellular and animal models, observational studies and clinical trials. Meal timing and dietary composition act as signals to peripheral clocks, while NAD+, sirtuins and AMP-activated protein kinase link nutrient availability with clock regulation and mitochondrial metabolism. We appraise time-restricted eating, protein distribution, NAD+ precursors, tryptophan- and melatonin-containing foods, magnesium, omega-3 fatty acids, polyphenols and fermentable fiber. Experimental findings provide mechanistic plausibility, but metabolic improvements and target engagement have not translated into demonstrated neuroprotection. Clinical application must account for levodopa-protein interactions, undernutrition, frailty and sarcopenia. Adequately powered trials with circadian-phase assessment, controlled energy intake and clinically meaningful neurological outcomes are required before a "circadian diet" can be established as a disease-modifying intervention.

papers.title: Interoceptive-autonomic pathways in mood state transitions in bipolar disorder: a hypothesis-generating brief review.
papers.abstract: Bipolar disorder is typically described in terms of clinical states such as depression, mania, or hypomania, but bodily signal processing, autonomic regulation, and emotion regulation across these states have not yet been integrated into a single testable model. This review distinguishes cross-sectional correlates of mood states from longitudinal predictors of subsequent mood changes. It proposes a state-dependent framework linking sleep-circadian disruption, autonomic flexibility, interoceptive processing, and emotion regulation; the temporal sequence and causal contributions of these components remain unestablished. Cross-sectional findings describe concurrent associations, recovery studies characterize changes accompanying symptom resolution, and prospective studies inform temporal ordering and prediction; none alone establishes a mechanism driving mood-state transitions. This article discusses direct evidence from bipolar disorder, transdiagnostic evidence, and theoretical inference in a hierarchical manner, without equating HRV with interoception or treating altered interoception as a single pathophysiological mechanism of bipolar disorder. Finally, it proposes a research protocol comprising state-stratified heartbeat discrimination/signal detection tasks, HRV reactivity and recovery, sleep and activity rhythms, ecological momentary assessment (EMA), and longitudinal assessment of state transitions.

papers.title: Epilepsy at the Airport.
papers.abstract: Limited data exists on which people, including those with epilepsy, are at increased risk of seizures during air travel and the contribution of specific travel-related triggers. We retrospectively reviewed attendances at our Epilepsy Rapid Access Clinic (RASC) over a 19-month period to identify patients presenting with seizures related to air travel. We also included patients identified by the epilepsy team who had not attended the clinic. Of 242 RASC attendees, nine patients (3.7%) had seizures associated with air travel. An additional nine patients were identified through other sources. All reported events were bilateral tonic-clonic seizures. Six (33%) patients had known epilepsy, of whom five had idiopathic generalised epilepsy (IGE). Four of these six patients had well-controlled epilepsy prior to the travel-related seizure relapse. Six (33%) patients were diagnosed with epilepsy after evaluation, including two with IGE. Twelve (67%) patients presented with seizures whilst awaiting departing flights, with a notable clustering around morning departures. Sleep deprivation was reported by 15 (83%) patients as a trigger. These findings suggest that patients with IGE may be at higher risk of seizures in these circumstances. The predominance of events in departure terminals, particularly before morning flights, highlights a potentially modifiable risk factor. Targeted counselling on modifiable risk factors may reduce risk and anxiety and should be incorporated into routine clinical care to support safer air travel. Thus, patients should be routinely educated about the potential of air travel as a seizure trigger.

papers.title: Contactless Oxygen Desaturation Prediction and Oxygen Desaturation Index (ODI) Estimation from Nocturnal Breathing Sounds via Deep Learning.
papers.abstract: Intermittent hypoxemia is increasingly recognized as a stronger predictor of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) than the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI). We developed a sound-based AI model to detect oxygen desaturation events and estimate the oxygen desaturation index (ODI) from nocturnal breathing sounds in a fully contactless manner. The model was trained using 2,973 nights of synchronized polysomnography (PSG) and audio recordings obtained from hospital- and home-based settings. Validation and independent testing were performed on 664 and 802 nights, respectively. Audio signals were converted into Mel spectrograms and processed using a Vision Transformer-based architecture. Performance was evaluated at the 30-second epoch level using sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1 score, accuracy, and Cohen's κ. ODI estimation was assessed using Pearson correlation, Bland-Altman analysis, mean absolute error (MAE), and root mean square error (RMSE). For epoch-by-epoch desaturation detection, the model achieved a sensitivity of 0.79, specificity of 0.95, precision of 0.78, F1 score of 0.79, overall accuracy of 0.92, and κ of 0.74. Estimated ODI showed agreement with PSG-derived ODI (r = 0.93, R² = 0.87, p < 0.001). Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated a mean bias of -0.29 events/h with 95% limits of agreement from -14.73 to 14.14 events/h. Breathing sound-based deep learning enables contactless detection of oxygen desaturation events and reliable ODI estimation. This approach may provide a scalable, non-contact method for sleep-disordered breathing assessment in real-world settings.

papers.title: The Case for Low-Friction High-Adherence Passive Sleep-Tracking Devices in Longitudinal Monitoring of Neurodegenerative Disease.
papers.abstract: Digital health technologies are playing an increasingly important role in patient monitoring, able to capture longitudinal data to supplement scheduled episodic evaluations conducted by clinicians. Rapid advances in sensors and data processing algorithms have resulted in some highly sophisticated systems capable of monitoring and tracking numerous symptoms with high levels of sensitivity and specificity. These approaches, however, often require active engagement with the patient, potentially increasing burden in a clinical trial and often resulting in diminishing adherence over time. In the case of slow-progressing neurodegenerative diseases, this may become an obstacle, as often very subtle changes in symptoms are typically monitored over a multi-year period. Accordingly, there is evident interest in passive monitoring solutions which have minimal burden on patients. Smart ring technologies are one such solution, with appealing form factors, low engagement requirements and increasing intervals before device recharging is required. While newer devices are capable of tracking sleep function with increasing levels of accuracy, they are unable to offer the precision afforded by gold standard sleep analysis such as electroencephalography (EEG), polysomnography (PSG) and sleep laboratory protocols. Prompted by a recent study which highlighted the reduced accuracy of consumer-based sleep devices compared with conventional approaches, we posit that the benefits of such devices may offset the constraints of measurement accuracy. Furthermore, any accuracy-adherence trade-offs would be compensated by long-term statistical benefits derived from detecting within-person changes and reducing measurement noise through enhanced sampling frequencies. In this perspective, we highlight their potential utility in tracking Parkinson's disease patients longitudinally, where compromised sleep architectures are associated with multiple symptoms and continuous monitoring could offer myriad patient benefits.

papers.title: Integrating Chronophysiological and Bioinformatic Perspectives on Nesfatin-1, Circadian Feeding Rhythms, and Cortisol Regulation.
papers.abstract: Nesfatin-1, a peptide derived from nucleobindin-2, regulates feeding, stress, and sleep-wake processes. To date, the available information suggests that nesfatin-1 is involved in stress regulation and colocalises with substances that influence cortisol, but the circadian interplay between nesfatin-1 and cortisol remains poorly defined. This review integrates biological timing, tissue-specific actions of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, and circadian misalignment, and is supported by in silico protein-association analysis. A structured database search retained relevant studies published from January 2006 to March 2026; heterogeneity necessitated narrative synthesis. Rodent experiments support effects of central NUCB2/nesfatin-1 on feeding and HPA-axis activation. Murine corticotroph experiments report increased POMC abundance, whereas an H295R human adrenocortical carcinoma-cell study reports reduced cortisol content and stimulated release. These findings concern different experimental systems and do not demonstrate coordinated central-adrenal regulation in vivo. The network analysis identified NPY and POMC as prominent nodes within the predefined candidate network, with enrichment of feeding- and HPA-axis-related pathways. Given the biologically targeted selection of input genes, these findings are interpreted as hypothesis-generating associations rather than independent confirmation of a regulatory mechanism. Within the literature examined in this review, direct evidence characterising the 24 h temporal profile of nesfatin-1 in humans, its phase relationship with cortisol, and potential alterations during circadian misalignment was not identified. This apparent evidence gap warrants further investigation through controlled, time-resolved human studies.

papers.title: Cannabinol for Sleep and Insomnia: A Critical Narrative Review and an Olive-Derived Polyphenol Combination Hypothesis.
papers.abstract: Cannabinol (CBN) is marketed for sleep, but its clinical evidence is limited and heterogeneous. This critical narrative review evaluates CBN-specific sleep studies and considers an olive-derived phenolic combination as a separate, untested clinical hypothesis. Three key randomized trials enrolled different populations and used oral doses of 20-300 mg over one night to four weeks. Primary sleep-quality or sleep-maintenance outcomes were not consistently positive; dose-ranging signals were multiplicity-sensitive and did not identify an optimal dose. At 300 mg, an acute insomnia trial reported selected secondary sleep benefits alongside next-day vigilance and simulated-driving concerns. Rodent findings implicate CBN and its metabolites, but route, exposure, tolerance and dependence limit extrapolation. Oleocanthal studies measured behavioral sleep in disease-model mice, whereas a human olive-phenol trial reported a fatigue benefit rather than a separately demonstrated sleep-domain effect. Parent phenolic instability, metabolism and uncertain target-site exposure weaken direct translation of micromolar assays. The proposed combination warrants exposure-informed investigation, not therapeutic endorsement. Progress requires product-specific safety and analytical qualification, component-controlled experiments and patient-prioritized outcomes alongside established insomnia care.

papers.title: Choroid plexus volume as a marker of chronotherapeutic responsiveness in major depressive disorder.
papers.abstract: Circadian rhythm disruption is a core feature of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD). The choroid plexus (ChP), a circadian-regulated structure involved in cerebrospinal fluid production and immune signalling, has been previously associated with depression and may undergo structural changes in response to chronotherapeutics. The study included 25 patients with MDD and 25 matched healthy controls who underwent MRI. Patients received total sleep deprivation plus light therapy (TSD + LT), consisting of three 36-hour sleep deprivation cycles, each separated by a night of recovery sleep. LT was administered for 30 min every morning. Depressive symptoms, sleep quality, and chronotype were assessed through Beck's Depression Inventory (BDI), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire (MEQ), respectively. ChP volumes were extracted with FreeSurfer and normalized for intracranial volume. Effects of chronotherapeutics were assessed on BDI, PSQI, and ChP volumes, with treatment response as a between-subject factor. The efficacy of treatment was also investigated stratifying for chronotype. Also, group differences in ChP volume and associations with sleep and BDI scores were explored. TSD + LT reduced depressive symptoms and improved sleep quality, with changes in PSQI associated with symptom improvement. Eveningness predicted greater depressive symptom reduction. At baseline, responders already exhibited larger left ChP volume than controls. Following treatment, a treatment × response interaction emerged for right ChP volume, showing a significant reduction in responders. Finally, reductions in both right and left ChP volumes predicted clinical improvement, and sleep quality improvement predicted right ChP volume reduction. This is the first study showing that chronotherapy modulates ChP structure in MDD, suggesting a link between circadian dysregulation and ChP enlargement proportional to clinical improvement and predicted by sleep amelioration. ChP volume may represent a biomarker of treatment responsiveness and circadian realignment.

papers.title: Detecting sleep deprivation from running biomechanics using machine learning classification: a comparison between wearable and laboratory motion capture.
papers.abstract: Sleep deprivation is associated with impaired endurance performance and an increased risk of running-related injury. Previous research has identified alterations in running biomechanics following a single night of sleep deprivation under laboratory conditions. However, whether these biomechanical changes can be detected using wearable technology remains unknown. Twenty-one recreationally active runners completed submaximal treadmill running under both normal sleep and total sleep deprivation conditions in a randomized crossover design. Biomechanical features were extracted simultaneously using a full-body motion capture system and a trunk-mounted wearable sensor. Five machine learning classifiers were evaluated in two classification tasks: a within-subject task using paired recordings from the same individual, and a between-subject task performed without individual baseline data. Within-subject classification exceeded chance level (label-permutation testing, p < 0.05 ) for most models and both measurement systems, with best accuracies of 84% for the wearable sensor (Logistic Regression) and 81% for the motion capture system (Random Forest). These findings indicate that sleep deprivation produces a systematic and individually consistent biomechanical signature during running. In contrast, between-subject classification failed across nearly all models and systems, with accuracies remaining close to chance level (˜50%), suggesting that inter-individual variability obscures the sleep-deprivation signal in the absence of personalized baseline data. Both systems converged on temporal organization, loading-related variables, and stride-to-stride variability as the most discriminative feature domains. Contrary to expectations, the laboratory motion capture system did not outperform the wearable sensor. Together, these findings suggest that individualized, baseline-referenced monitoring may be important for detecting sleep-deprivation-related changes in running gait, and suggest that a single trunk-mounted wearable sensor may provide a practical solution for real-world monitoring when paired recordings are available.

papers.title: Scalp high-frequency oscillations differentiate neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy with and without electroencephalographically confirmed seizures.
papers.abstract: Hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) is a leading cause of neonatal seizures, but seizure detection is challenging when continuous electroencephalography (EEG) is unavailable and neonates undergo only a single routine EEG. Biomarkers derived from routine EEG may aid identification of neonates with seizures. We investigated whether scalp high-frequency oscillation (HFO) rates derived from the first eligible routine EEG (1) differentiate neonates with HIE with and without seizures; and (2) contribute to seizure classification alongside established clinical, neurophysiological, and imaging biomarkers. We retrospectively analyzed routine scalp EEG recordings from 33 term neonates with HIE (17 with seizures, 16 without), obtained at a mean postnatal age of 4 ± 3 days. The mean analyzed EEG duration was 38 ± 14 min in neonates with seizures and 36 ± 20 min in those without. HFO rates in sleep segments were quantified using a validated automated detector. Scalp HFO rates were significantly higher in neonates with seizures than in those without (.12 ± .11 vs. .03 ± .02 HFOs/min/channel, adjusted p = .02). An HFO rate threshold of .07 HFOs/min/channel optimally discriminated neonates who had seizures from those who did not (area under the curve [AUC] = .81). HFO rates did not differ significantly according to HIE severity, therapeutic hypothermia, antiseizure medication response, EEG background activity, or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) abnormalities. Multivariable models incorporating HFO rate, EEG background activity, and MRI findings showed discrimination (AUC = .92, 95% confidence interval [CI] = .69-1.00 for logistic regression; AUC = 1.00, 95% CI = .75-1.00 for random forest), with HFO rate as the strongest contributor to seizure classification. These findings support scalp HFO rate as a potential electrophysiological biomarker of seizure occurrence in neonatal HIE, complementary to EEG background assessment and MRI findings. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether HFOs can predict subsequent seizures.

papers.title: EEG Microstate Alterations and Their Association with Cognitive Performance in Late-Onset Epilepsy of Unknown Etiology: Comparison with Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: Cognitive impairment is common in late-onset epilepsy of unknown etiology (LOEU), but its electrophysiological correlates and relationship to Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain unclear. We compared resting-state electroencephalogram (EEG) microstate dynamics among LOEU, AD, and cognitively normal (CN) groups and examined their associations with cognitive performance. Eyes-closed 32-channel resting-state EEG recordings were analyzed from 60 patients with LOEU, 65 with AD, and 60 CN participants. Four canonical microstate classes (A-D) were identified. Group differences in microstate parameters were tested with false discovery rate correction. Associations with Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores were examined using multivariable interaction models adjusted for age, sex, education, and cerebral small vessel disease burden. Microstate B duration was longer in LOEU and AD than in CN (Holm-adjusted p=0.011 and 0.016), whereas microstate C occurrence was lower in both patient groups (p=0.001 and 0.018). Microstate D duration was longer in LOEU than in CN and AD (both p=0.038). For microstate A duration, the group interaction survived false discovery rate correction for MMSE (q=0.0255) but not MoCA (q=0.122). In LOEU, longer microstate A duration was associated with lower MoCA and MMSE scores. Pairwise slope comparisons were more negative in LOEU than in CN for both outcomes, whereas LOEU-AD slope differences were not significant. LOEU showed altered resting-state EEG microstate dynamics that partly overlapped with those observed in AD, alongside a group difference in microstate D duration. Microstate A duration was associated with cognitive performance in LOEU, although this association did not significantly differ from that observed in AD. These findings support further investigation of EEG microstates as electrophysiological correlates of cognitive dysfunction in LOEU while also highlighting overlap with AD.

papers.title: White matter microstructure and hyperintensity burden in isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder.
papers.abstract: Isolated rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder represents a prodromal phase of α-synucleinopathy. Diffusion MRI provides in vivo markers of white matter microstructural properties, while white matter hyperintensities reflect cerebrovascular injury. However, their relative contributions to cognitive and clinical dysfunctions in patients with isolated rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder remain unclear. We analysed 168 polysomnography-confirmed isolated rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder participants from the North American Prodromal Synucleinopathy Consortium. Multi-shell diffusion MRI was used to derive metrics from diffusion tensor imaging (fractional anisotropy and mean diffusivity) and Neurite Orientation Dispersion and Density Imaging (tissue-weighted neurite density index and orientation dispersion index) across 39 white matter regions using a modified Johns Hopkins University white matter atlas. White matter hyperintensity burden was quantified from fluid-attenuated inversion recovery MRI. Using linear regression adjusted for age and sex, we compared white matter microstructure and hyperintensity burden between clinically impaired and unimpaired participants and examined associations with multiple cognitive and clinical domains, including global cognition, working memory, motor severity, manual dexterity, autonomic dysfunction, olfactory function, prodromal disease severity and daytime sleepiness. False discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied to account for multiple comparisons. In our sample (n = 168), participants with clinical impairment (n = 57) demonstrated higher white matter hyperintensity burden than unimpaired participants (n = 111) and showed limited microstructural differences, including lower fractional anisotropy in the superior fronto-occipital fasciculus and inferior occipital white matter and higher orientation dispersion index in inferior occipital white matter. After adjusting for white matter hyperintensity burden, only increased occipital orientation dispersion index remained statistically significant. Diffusion metrics showed widespread associations with digit span forward performance and autonomic dysfunction. In contrast, increased white matter hyperintensity burden demonstrated broader associations with poorer Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores, poorer digit span forward performance, lower Purdue Pegboard performance and higher Prodromal Synucleinopathy Rating Scale scores, indicating greater prodromal disease severity. Our findings highlight cerebrovascular white matter burden as an important correlate of clinical dysfunction in isolated rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder and underscore the need to consider cerebrovascular lesions when interpreting diffusion imaging markers in prodromal synucleinopathy.

papers.title: Postoperative Delirium Across the Perioperative Pathway: A Structured Narrative Review of Clinical Maturity and Implementation Priorities.
papers.abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a highly prevalent but frequently underrecognized complication that disproportionately affects frail and older surgical patients. This structured narrative review aims to synthesize contemporary evidence on adult postoperative delirium across the perioperative pathway and to classify major preventive and therapeutic strategies according to clinical maturity, target population, and implementation readiness. A structured literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) and Web of Science Core Collection was performed, supplemented by ClinicalTrials.gov, official ESAIC and ASA resources, reference-list screening, and selected seminal pre-2021 publications. Current evidence supports a multifactorial model in which baseline cognitive and physiological vulnerability interacts with inflammatory, pharmacological, hemodynamic, nociceptive, sleep-related, and environmental stressors. No single anesthetic technique, processed-EEG target, blood-pressure threshold, cerebral oximetry strategy, or pharmacological agent consistently prevents POD across surgical populations. Multicomponent non-pharmacological prevention has the most consistent support, whereas dexmedetomidine and other pharmacological approaches appear context-dependent, and biomarkers and metabolic targets remain investigational. Future progress will depend on standardized delirium ascertainment, better phenotyping, multimodal prediction and prevention strategies, and reliable implementation systems that identify vulnerability early and maintain effective preventive care across transitions.

papers.title: EEG Biomarkers for Stress Detection: A Comparative Analysis of Hjorth Parameters, Spectral and Fractal-Dimension Measures.
papers.abstract: EEG-based stress detection is increasingly relevant for intelligent sensing and human-computer interaction, particularly for systems that aim to adapt to users' changing cognitive and affective states. While conventional EEG-based stress detection approaches mainly rely on spectral band-power features, fractal-dimension measures and Hjorth parameters may provide additional information about underlying brain dynamics. However, their relative contribution, spatial distribution, and frequency-band dependence remain insufficiently understood. In this study, pre-recorded EEG data from a stress-inducing experiment were analyzed using statistical feature pre-selection and multiple machine-learning classifiers. The contribution of different EEG features was evaluated across participants, while scalp topographical maps were used to characterize the spatial distribution of informative features. The results identify Hjorth activity, frontal β asymmetry, and the γ/θ ratio as among the most frequently selected features in the ANOVA-based feature-selection analysis. Combined feature-space configurations including Hjorth parameters and fractal-dimension measures achieved higher classification performance than the conventional-feature reference configuration. These findings provide further insight into the spatial and frequency-specific characteristics of EEG features associated with the investigated stress-inducing cognitive task and demonstrate the value of combining conventional spectral features with Hjorth parameters and fractal-dimension measures for physiological-state sensing. The proposed approach may support the development of computationally efficient EEG-based monitoring of stress-related cognitive states for intelligent and adaptive human-computer interaction, including neuroadaptive and context-aware systems.

papers.title: Circadian Rhythm-Related Characteristics and Adiposity in Relation to CAP-Defined Hepatic Steatosis Among Shift and Non-Shift Workers: A Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide and linked to shift work. This study aimed to investigate the associations of circadian rhythm, sleep characteristics, anthropometric measures, and adiposity-related parameters with controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) values, and to assess their independent associations and sex-specific discriminatory performance in identifying hepatic steatosis among shift and non-shift workers. Methods: A total of 436 workers (328 men and 108 women), aged 19-64 years, from seven large-scale tea factories in Rize, Türkiye, were included. Social jetlag (SJL) and eating jetlag (EJL) were calculated from workday-free-day differences in sleep and meal timing, respectively, and sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Multivariable linear regression and sex-specific receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed. Results: Mean SJL (p = 0.017) and the distribution of SJL categories (p = 0.022) differed significantly between female shift and non-shift workers, whereas neither differed in men (p = 0.827 and p = 0.542, respectively). These comparisons are exploratory because SJL and EJL estimates are not directly comparable across rotating shift assignments or between shift and non-shift workers. CAP values and the prevalence of CAP-defined hepatic steatosis did not differ significantly by shift-work status in either sex. CAP was positively correlated with anthropometric and adiposity-related measures, with the strongest adjusted correlations observed for waist circumference, abdominal volume index (AVI), BMI, and body fat mass (all rs = 0.66, p < 0.001). In the fully adjusted regression model, age, BMI, and neck circumference were independently associated with higher CAP values, whereas SJL, EJL, sleep duration, and PSQI total score were not. In sex-specific ROC analyses, waist circumference and AVI showed the highest discriminatory performance in men (both AUC = 0.86), whereas BMI showed the highest discriminatory performance in women (AUC = 0.81). SJL and EJL did not significantly discriminate hepatic steatosis in either sex, while sleep duration showed weak discrimination in women (AUC = 0.63, q = 0.042). Conclusions: Anthropometric and adiposity-related measures were strongly associated with CAP values and showed good sex-specific discriminatory performance for hepatic steatosis. However, SJL findings, particularly comparisons by shift-work status, should be considered exploratory given the limited comparability of SJL and EJL estimates among rotating shift workers and between shift and non-shift workers. These simple, readily obtainable anthropometric measurements and derived adiposity indices may facilitate preliminary risk stratification for hepatic steatosis in occupational settings.

papers.title: Associations of short and long sleep duration with multiple adverse health outcomes among ageing adults in South Africa.
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to assess the longitudinal associations between short and long sleep duration with multiple adverse health outcomes (mortality, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, functional limitations, depressive symptoms, loneliness, posttraumatic stress (PTSD) symptoms, impaired cognition, dynapenia, addominal obesity, dynapenic abdominal obesity, and general obesity) among community-residents 40 years and older, also broken down by sex. Data from three waves of the "Health and Ageing in Africa: A Longitudinal Study of an INDEPTH Community in South Africa (HAALSI)" (2015-2022) were utilized. There were 10483 observations of people who were 40 years of age or older. The American National Sleep Foundation was used to measure self-reported sleep duration. The association between sleep duration and 7-year mortality was assessed using hazard ratios. The longitudinal relationships between short and long sleep duration (using normal or recommended sleep length as a reference) and unfavorable health outcomes were estimated using linear, conditional, and multinomial logistic fixed effects (FE) regressions. This study showed an association between short sleep duration and mortality, hypertension, depressive symptoms, and cardiovascular disease, while there were no significant associations between short sleep duration and diabetes, functional limitations, loneliness, PTSD symptoms, impaired cognition, dynapenia, abdominal obesity, dynapenic abdominal obesity and general obesity. Furthermore, this study found an association between long sleep duration and functional limitations, depressive symptoms, loneliness, PTSD symptoms, impaired or lower cognition, dynapenia, abdominal obesity, dynapenic abdominal obesity and general obesity, while there were no significant associations between long sleep duration and mortality, cardiovascular disease, hypertension, and diabetes. Short sleep duration was associated with four and long sleep duration with nine adverse health outcomes. The results can be applied to health literacy and education initiatives to promote getting adequate sleep, which is a crucial aspect of total sleep health. Future studies from other countries are recommended.

papers.title: Simultaneous EEG-fMRI in major depressive disorder: A systematic review of brain networks, neurovascular coupling, and clinical correlates.
papers.abstract: Simultaneous electroencephalography-functional magnetic resonance imaging (EEG-fMRI) offers unique potential to characterize brain network dysfunction and neurovascular coupling in major depressive disorder (MDD). However, the field lacks a rigorous synthesis restricted to strictly defined MDD populations with true multimodal integration. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261292902), we searched PubMed, Scopus, CENTRAL, and Google Scholar (inception to March 2026) for simultaneous EEG-fMRI studies in adults (≥18 years) with MDD. We excluded subclinical samples, healthy-only populations, and sequential acquisitions to ensure diagnostic specificity. Primary outcomes were network dysfunction, neurovascular coupling, and clinical associations. Narrative synthesis was performed due to data paucity (<3 studies/outcome). Risk of bias was assessed using modified ROB2, ROBINS-I, and JBI tools. Nine studies (eight cohorts; N=377) met strict criteria. Two reports from one cohort investigating anhedonia via neurofeedback (Zotev et al.) showed moderate-to-strong correlations between EEG-fMRI metrics and severity (r = 0.47 and 0.69). Single-study findings reported effect sizes for anxiety (r = 0.74), depression change (r = -0.38 to 0.90), and rumination (r = 0.20). Analytical heterogeneity was substantial. Evidence certainty was low due to bias risk and imprecision. Small sample sizes, methodological fragmentation, and reliance on single cohorts for specific outcomes limit generalizability. Simultaneous EEG-fMRI identifies strong neurophysiological correlates (e.g., anhedonia, treatment response) in active contexts (e.g., neurofeedback, ketamine), but evidence for generalizable resting-state biomarkers remains insufficient. Future efforts must prioritize standardized pipelines and large-scale cohorts to transition this technique to a clinical biomarker.

papers.title: Short-term physiological responses to nocturnal pressurization in male high-altitude workers: an exploratory pilot randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: This exploratory pilot randomized controlled trial investigated whether a nocturnal pressurization intervention, designed to simulate altitude reduction during sleep, was associated with changes in multi-system physiological responses in male workers with chronic intermittent high-altitude exposure. Twenty-four male workers were randomized to a Pressurization group (n = 12) or a control group (n = 12); Over a 5-week protocol, the Pressurization group slept at the simulated altitudes while both groups worked at 3500 m. The primary outcome was mean nocturnal peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2); secondary outcomes were ambulatory blood pressure (BP), serum normetanephrine and metanephrine, Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System components, and oxidative stress markers. The intervention was associated with short-term changes, the largest of which occurred during the 2000 m-simulated week. SpO2 was higher than in controls at 2500 m and 2000 m (both p < 0.001). Nocturnal diastolic BP was lower at 2500 m (- 7.25 mmHg, p = 0.024), normetanephrine, metanephrine and angiotensin II were reduced at 2000 m (Ang II: -23.10 pg/mL, p = 0.011), and 8-iso-PGF2α was lower with higher total antioxidant capacity at both altitudes. None of these differences persisted at the fifth-week recovery assessment. A nocturnal pressurization intervention simulating descent to 2000 m was associated with improved nocturnal oxygenation and short-term reductions in neurohormonal and oxidative stress in male high-altitude workers. The changes were reversible and had disappeared one week after the intervention ceased; they should therefore not be interpreted as an improvement in long-term adaptation, and the study should be regarded as hypothesis-generating.

papers.title: Spontaneous Parturition at Term Is Governed by Endogenous Circadian Rhythms Rather Than Geophysical or Meteorological Factors: A Historical Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Pervasive folklore suggests that lunar phases and acute weather shifts trigger spontaneous labor onset and membrane rupture, contributing to heightened maternal anxiety and influencing labor ward staffing. We evaluated potential associations between astronomical lunar phases, barometric pressure fluctuations, and extreme heat events with spontaneous labor onset and premature rupture of membranes (PROM). A historical cohort study was conducted at an urban tertiary academic center (1998-2022), analyzing 21,538 spontaneous, singleton, term deliveries. Birth records were linked to regional hourly barometric pressure, Heat Index (HI), sunshine duration, and eight astronomical lunar phases. Primary outcomes were daily spontaneous delivery count, the timing of birth across the 24-h cycle, and the occurrence of PROM. Multivariable Poisson and logistic regression models were applied, controlling for maternal age, parity, and birthweight. Spontaneous births were uniformly distributed across lunar phases, showing no increase during the Full Moon compared with the New Moon (IRR 1.01, 95% CI 0.94-1.09, p = 0.698). Days characterized by significant meteorological variance (barometric drops > 8 hPa; IRR 1.01, 95% CI 0.98-1.04, p = 0.459) and thermal stress (IRR 1.00, 95% CI 0.99-1.00, p = 0.484) were not associated with delivery frequency. Lunar cycles did not influence PROM incidence (p = 0.771; Full Moon aOR 0.77, 95% CI 0.56-1.07). Conversely, spontaneous deliveries demonstrated a robust endogenous circadian rhythm peaking at midday (11:00 AM-12:00 PM), consistent across weekdays, weekends, and parity subgroups. Spontaneous delivery timing at term appears to be governed by an endogenous circadian rhythm (likely reflecting nocturnal labor onset) rather than extrinsic lunar or meteorological triggers. Antenatal counseling can reassure families that parturition is guided by an intrinsic biological cadence rather than ambient fluctuations, while perinatal resources should align with circadian demand.

papers.title: Thermally provoked itch in atopic dermatitis: current evidence, knowledge gaps, and digital approaches to nocturnal scratching.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease in which pruritus significantly contributes to sleep disturbance, impaired quality of life, and the itch-scratch cycle. Heat, sweating, hot-water exposure, and nocturnal occlusion are frequently reported as itch-aggravating factors, although these exposures are biologically heterogeneous. This narrative review critically examines the current clinical relevance, mechanistic evidence, and objective monitoring of thermally provoked itch in AD. Thermosensitive ion channels, epithelial cytokines, neuropeptides, dermal fibroblast-derived artemin, and altered peripheral and central sensory processing provide a plausible framework for thermally provoked itch. However, the relative contribution of these pathways to heat-aggravated itch in humans remains incompletely defined. Digital monitoring technologies, including wrist-worn actigraphy, smartwatch-based algorithms, hand-mounted sensors, non-wearable systems, thermal imaging, acoustic sensing, and multimodal devices, are increasingly used to quantify scratch duration, frequency, intensity, and sleep-related patterns in real-world settings. These tools do not replace patient-reported outcomes, but they may provide an objective behavioral layer for assessing otherwise hidden nocturnal burden and monitoring changes over time. Future prospective studies should define heat-responsive clinical characteristics, standardize nocturnal scratch endpoints, validate digital measures across pediatric and adult populations, and jointly assess thermal and humidity exposure, skin temperature, itch, scratching, sleep, skin-barrier status, disease severity, and relevant confounders. Such studies are needed to determine whether thermal exposure independently predicts clinically meaningful nocturnal scratching and to establish the clinical value of digital scratch-monitoring endpoints in AD. Integrating mechanistic insights with objective monitoring may support more precise assessment and patient-centered management of AD.

Mood-product use rose along a gradient of psychological burden, from frequent stress (adjusted odds ratios [aOR] 1.80, 95% confidence intervals [CI] 1.72-1.88) through work-related exhaustion (2.17, 2.08-2.26) and poor self-rated mental health (2.44, 2.34-2.55) to a lifetime depression diagnosis (2.53, 2.41-2.65). A lifetime depression diagnosis also co-occurred with sleep (1.92, 1.83-2.01) and memory-product use (1.77, 1.69-1.85), while multivitamin and hair/skin use stayed flat (aOR ≈ 1.0). The scope of these findings is set by two features: the depression measure is lifetime, not an assessment of current symptoms, and the questionnaire recorded the purpose of use, not the product identity, ingredients or dose.

papers.title: Lesion-directed quantitative EEG after reperfusion therapy is associated with malignant cerebral edema and functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke: a prospective exploratory cohort study.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke causes electrophysiological slowing within minutes which may precede detectable structural changes, making electroencephalography (EEG) a sensitive bedside marker of tissue at risk. Prior quantitative EEG (qEEG) studies often averaged bilateral or frontal activity, focused on thrombectomy, and were recorded at 24 h. We tested whether a lesion-directed alpha-to-delta ratio (lesion-ADR) within 72 h after reperfusion is associated with malignant cerebral edema (MCE) and functional outcomes. In a prospective single-center cohort of anterior-circulation ischemic stroke treated with intravenous alteplase (IV-rtPA), endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), or both, a 7-min EEG was obtained ≤72 h after reperfusion. Lesion-ADR was defined as the mean ADR of ipsilesional electrodes; the reperfusion-to-EEG interval (ΔT) was recorded. The primary outcome was MCE (midline shift ≥5 mm and/or decompressive hemicraniectomy). Secondary outcomes were favorable functional outcomes at discharge and 90 days (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2). Model discrimination was assessed using ROC analysis and AUC with bootstrap internal validation. Adjusted associations were assessed using parsimonious Firth penalized logistic regression models. Forty-nine patients were included. For MCE, the combined lesion-ADR + ΔT model achieved an apparent AUC of 0.888 (95% CI 0.765-0.960); bootstrap internal validation yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.889. For discharge independence (mRS ≤ 2; n = 9), the ADR-only model showed an apparent AUC of 0.899. Lesion-ADR remained associated with favorable outcome after separate adjustment for admission NIHSS (OR 1.438 per 0.1-unit increase; p = 0.009) and reperfusion treatment modality (OR 1.367; p = 0.022). For 90-day independence (n = 13), the ADR-only AUC was 0.759 (95% CI 0.615-0.869) and the ADR-only model showed moderate discrimination for 90-day functional independence. The association with 90-day outcome was attenuated after accounting for admission NIHSS (OR 1.245 per 0.1-unit increase; p = 0.088). A brief lesion-directed ADR obtained within 72 h after reperfusion was associated with functional outcomes, while its combination with EEG timing showed encouraging discrimination for MCE in this cohort. These exploratory findings suggest lesion-directed qEEG may serve as a potential adjunctive biomarker after reperfusion therapy and warrant validation in larger cohorts.

papers.title: EEG-Based Recognition of Self-Imagined Emotions Using Multi-Domain Features and Subject-Specific Calibration.
papers.abstract: Self-imagined emotional imagery, in which individuals internally generate emotional states without external induction, plays a key role in shaping affective brain-computer interface (BCI) systems. Robust generalization across individuals is challenging due to significant variability in EEG patterns. This study evaluates a multi-domain electroencephalography (EEG) decoding framework for self-imagined emotion recognition, integrating time-frequency features, functional connectivity, effective connectivity, and subject-specific calibration. EEG data were collected from 38 participants and categorized into four emotional conditions using the valence-arousal model. Time-frequency features were extracted using the wavelet transform; functional connectivity was assessed using the phase locking value (PLV) and Pearson's correlation; and effective connectivity was estimated using Granger causality. For comparison, a two-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) based on the continuous wavelet transform was implemented. Under pooled sample-wise cross-validation, PLV-based features combined with a support vector machine (SVM) achieved 97.0% accuracy, while the CNN reached 94.75%. Under leave-one-subject-out evaluation, accuracy declined to approximately 25-30%, indicating limited generalization to unseen participants. With subject-specific calibration using 75% of the target participant's data, the SVM achieved 95.0% accuracy. The results support the recognition of four emotional conditions under the evaluated protocol when data from the target participant are available. However, cross-subject generalizability remains a significant limitation. As the study was conducted under controlled experimental conditions, further research involving independent populations and experimental settings is necessary to evaluate the framework's robustness and applicability.

papers.title: A Lightweight Hybrid-Attention Conformer for Affective State Recognition from Wearable EEG.
papers.abstract: Recognizing affective states from electroencephalography (EEG) is a core task in affective computing, with applications in mental health monitoring and public safety. Most existing approaches rely on handcrafted features or image-based transformations of EEG, while transformer models capture global context at high computational cost. This study proposes KimiFormer, an end-to-end hybrid-attention Conformer that classifies raw EEG directly. A hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Stemming (STS) module tokenizes the multichannel signal and learns inter-electrode relationships. Stacked Conformer blocks combine linear and full attention in a 3:1 ratio, reducing computational cost while preserving long-range modeling. The model was evaluated on the public EEG Violence Dataset, recorded with a 14-channel wearable headset from 14 participants viewing violent and neutral videos. Under record-wise leave-one-record-out cross-validation with nested selection of the training hyperparameters, KimiFormer achieved 95.5% accuracy (97.0% under 10-fold cross-validation). On the external DREAMER dataset, its subject-independent performance remained close to chance (balanced accuracy 52.7% for valence and 50.2% for arousal), as did that of two established raw-EEG models. Ablation showed the STS module to be essential (65% accuracy without it). With 3.2 M parameters, 1.51 GFLOPs and an inference latency of 15.64 ms per sample, KimiFormer is suited to real-time, on-device processing of low-channel wearable EEG.

papers.title: [Digital media use and dependencies in adolescence: Psychological and mental health perspectives, regulatory dilemmas, and preventive considerations].
papers.abstract: Adolescents' digital presence is no longer merely a lifestyle phenomenon but a developmental, social-psychological, and mental health environment. Social media, short-video platforms, online gaming, and constant online availability have become major contexts for mood regulation, identity formation, peer embeddedness, and self-evaluation. This manuscript provides a narrative and integrative review of recent international and Hungarian literature. It discusses the psychological structure of problematic digital use, its mood-related, attentional, sleep-related, and interpersonal correlates, as well as regulatory and preventive issues from developmental, mental health, and phenomenological perspectives. The literature suggests that problematic digital use should not be equated with high frequency of use alone, but is better understood in terms of loss of control, functional impairment, and the outsourcing of affect regulation. In vulnerable adolescents, digital engagement may be associated with depressive and anxiety symptoms, poorer sleep, attentional instability, intensified social comparison, and increasingly externalized self-worth. Hungarian findings also indicate that digital media use is embedded in family and broader social ecology. Prevention and early intervention should not rely on a single restrictive or permissive policy measure, but rather on a coordinated system of platform responsibility, family and school containment, digital literacy, and early clinical recognition.

papers.title: The association between physical activity and academic procrastination among college students: the mediating role of self-efficacy and the moderating role of sleep quality.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the associations between physical activity and academic procrastination among college students within a cross-sectional framework while examining the mediating role of self-efficacy and the moderating role of sleep quality. A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 428 college students from universities in Shanghai. Participants completed the International Physical Activity Questionnaire-Short Form (IPAQ-S), the Academic Procrastination Scale, the General Self-Efficacy Scale (GSES), and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Data were analyzed using the PROCESS macro in SPSS 26.0 to test a moderated mediation model, adjusting for demographic covariates, including gender, age, academic major, academic year, only-child status, and geographic origin. (1) Physical activity was significantly and negatively associated with academic procrastination (β = -0.127, 95% confidence interval [CI] [-0.223, -0.031], p < 0.05) and positively associated with self-efficacy (β = 0.200, 95% CI [0.103, 0.296], p < 0.001). Self-efficacy was concurrently and negatively associated with procrastination (β = -0.235, 95% CI [-0.330, -0.142], p < 0.001). (2) Self-efficacy accounted for a significant portion of the association between physical activity and academic procrastination, with a significant indirect effect of -0.047 (95% CI [-0.078, -0.019]), accounting for 27.01% of the total effect. (3) Sleep quality significantly moderated the association between physical activity and self-efficacy (β = -0.147, 95% CI [-0.236, -0.056], p < 0.01) and the direct association between physical activity and academic procrastination (β = 0.147, 95% CI [0.058, 0.236], p < 0.01). (4) Conditional process analyses revealed that the indirect effect via self-efficacy and the direct association with procrastination were significant only among students with average or good sleep quality, but not among those with poor sleep quality. The findings reveal significant concurrent associations among physical activity, self-efficacy, sleep quality, and academic procrastination. Self-efficacy partially accounted for the relationship between physical activity and procrastination. Crucially, sleep quality emerged as a critical boundary condition: the linkages between physical activity and reduced procrastination (both direct and indirect) were evident only when sleep quality was adequate. These results underscore the necessity of adopting a stratified approach in future interventions-targeting physical activity and self-efficacy for adequately rested students, while integrating sleep hygiene support for those with poor sleep-pending validation through longitudinal or experimental designs.

papers.title: Translating Geroscience Into Clinical Practice: Molecular Targets, Emerging Therapies, and Lifestyle Strategies for Healthy Longevity.
papers.abstract: Population aging has intensified interest in interventions that preserve function and delay multiple chronic diseases by modifying the biology of aging. The field now spans molecular geroscience, experimental therapeutics, biomarker development, and preventive medicine, but the maturity of evidence varies substantially. This study aimed to synthesize foundational mechanisms, clinical and translational strategies, and lifestyle determinants relevant to healthy longevity, while distinguishing established practice from emerging or unproven interventions. A critical narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE and reference lists was conducted from January 2000 through August 2026. Priority was given to consensus frameworks, human randomized trials, prospective cohorts, systematic reviews, and influential mechanistic studies. Evidence was interpreted according to study design, clinical relevance, reproducibility, and safety. The expanded 12-hallmark framework depicts aging as an interconnected network involving genomic damage, impaired maintenance systems, maladaptive stress responses, inflammation, and dysbiosis. Senolytics, epigenetic reprogramming, nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) augmentation, mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibition, metformin, and spermidine are biologically plausible, but none yet has definitive evidence of extending lifespan in healthy humans. Epigenetic clocks are useful research biomarkers, although a lower clock estimate is not synonymous with rejuvenation or proven risk reduction. By contrast, cardiorespiratory fitness, muscle strength, dietary quality, restorative and regular sleep, avoidance of tobacco, management of cardiometabolic risk, and social connection are supported by much stronger human-outcome evidence. Responsible longevity medicine should integrate geroscience with rigorous preventive care, use biomarkers as adjuncts rather than diagnoses, and reserve experimental geroprotectors for well-designed trials. The near-term opportunity is not radical life extension, but compression of morbidity through scalable, equitable, and evidence-based preservation of health span.

papers.title: Acupuncture-Assisted Zolpidem Tartrate Tapering and Discontinuation in Patients with Chronic Insomnia Disorder Stabilized on Zolpidem: A Study Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: The prevalence of chronic insomnia disorder (CID) is relatively high and increases with age. The use of sedatives, along with the incidence of their adverse effects, is also rising, which can easily lead to health risks and negative outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of acupuncture-assisted zolpidem tartrate tapering and discontinuation in patients with CID whose insomnia symptoms are clinically stable while taking zolpidem. Additionally, this research may offer useful references for patients with CID seeking to safely and effectively reduce or discontinue zolpidem tartrate. These findings may inform future clinical research and larger multicenter confirmatory studies. papers.title: Promotion and economic considerations of domestic Vagus nerve stimulation within the Chinese three-tier epilepsy center system.
papers.abstract: Epilepsy affects approximately 10 million people in China, with about 30% developing drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). Vagus Nerve Stimulation (VNS) is an established neuromodulation therapy for DRE. Domestic VNS devices completed clinical trials in 2014 and entered clinical use in 2016. This study synthesizes clinical outcomes, promotion pathways, and economic considerations of domestic VNS devices within the Chinese three-tier epilepsy center network established by the China Association Against Epilepsy (CAAE). This narrative synthesis integrates data from previously published multicenter prospective real-world studies, CAAE accreditation records, market research, and health economics literature. Clinical outcome data were derived from studies encompassing 124 adult and 87 pediatric patients with DRE across 86 epilepsy centers. A cost comparison between domestic and imported VNS devices was performed based on market data and implantation volumes from 2022-2025. In adults, responder rates (≥50% seizure reduction) increased progressively from 35.4% at 1 month to 76.6% at 12 months post-implantation, with seizure-free rates reaching 10.9%. In pediatric patients, according to the available follow-up data, ≥50% responder rates (combining seizure freedom, 75% reduction, and 50% reduction) were 43.4% at visit 2, 40.6% at visit 3, 56.6% at visit 4, and 55.8% at visit 5; seizure freedom rates ranged from 1.1 to 9.3% across visits. Significant improvements were observed in sleep quality (PSQI: 5.43 → 4.44), depression (NDDI-E: 6.49 → 4.83), anxiety (GAD-7: 7.15 → 4.95), and quality of life (QOLIE-31: 54.40 → 61.33). Adverse events were mild and transient, primarily voice changes (20.3%) and cough (8.6%). The three-tier network comprises 526 centers (45 Tier-3, 259 Tier-2, 222 Tier-1) with standardized protocols and telemedicine platforms. Domestic VNS demonstrates encouraging efficacy, favorable safety, and improvements in comorbidities in both adult and pediatric DRE populations within the CAAE three-tier network. The network provides a structured framework for standardized application. However, the evidence is limited by the uncontrolled design of the primary studies, short follow-up, and the absence of a formal cost-effectiveness analysis. Prospective comparative clinical and economic validation is warranted.
